accuracy.evidence: Checked against Development Matters (DfE 2021) Reception PSED 'know and talk about the different factors that support their overall health and wellbeing ... toothbrushing', DfE Relationships, Sex and Health Education statutory guidance (primary health education: dental health and regular check-ups at the dentist), NHS 'Taking your child to the dentist' (go when milk teeth first appear), NICE CG19 dental recall (3 to 12 months for under-18s), NHS 'How to take your child's temperature' (digital thermometer in the armpit for under-5s) and NHS 'Baby teeth' (20 milk teeth; adults up to 32). Tool roles are stated plainly: stethoscope listens to heart and breathing, otoscope looks in the ear, dental mirror shows the backs of teeth. The safeguarding line (parent or carer stays, the clinician says what they will do and asks first) follows NSPCC PANTS guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented worries named in the adult text: a visit as punishment ('Because I was naughty' refused with 'punish', m9, family tip against using the dentist as a threat), going only when something hurts ('onlysick', prediction 1, p1), staying quiet about pain to be brave (Keep still on the sore tooth is refused with 'hide', prediction 3, p3), shutting the mouth, hiding or keeping a worry secret ('hideaway', 'secret' on the worry meter and in the challenge), tools that hurt (prediction 2: each tool's message says it only looks or listens) and mixing up tools ('tool'), plus 32 vs 20 teeth ('adult').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdocvisit is built round the visit itself: sorting reasons for a visit, ordering the four parts of a visit, dragging a stethoscope, ear light, thermometer and dentist mirror to leader-line chips on a body diagram, a dentist mirror that steps tooth by tooth across a row of five teeth where Keep still is refused only on the sore tooth and Hand up is the right signal, and a four-step worry meter. 1006 Medicines and household products: ask first (flagmeds), 858 Telling a grown-up when something feels wrong (flagtrust) and 924 Types of teeth (flagteeth, tooth shapes and jobs) use none of these mechanics. Shingle similarity to every other flag_*.js is under 30% (gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea comes from doing: the naughty and never-go cards bounce back with the reason; the visit cards only drop in sequence, so the child rehearses what will happen; each tool only lands on the place it checks and then says what it does and that it does not hurt; the mirror moves on only while teeth feel fine, and the sore tooth needs a hand up (a hand up on a fine tooth is accepted as a rest, not a mistake, so asking for a break is never punished); the worry meter falls only for helpful actions.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Yes, only when it hurts' (the never-go card is refused: check-ups find problems early), 'Yes, it pokes you' for the stethoscope (dropping it on the chest says it listens and does not hurt), and 'Yes, keep quiet' about a sore tooth (Keep still on the sore tooth is refused: the dentist may not know).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions with distinct slip messages, checked in the browser: punish ('A visit is never a punishment'), onlysick, hide, shut ('If you shut your mouth, the dentist cannot see or help'), hideaway, secret ('A worry is not a secret to keep'), tool (names what the stethoscope or thermometer really does), adult ('32 is for grown-ups') and count ('10 on top and 10 on the bottom').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs score -0.9 to 2.4 Flesch-Kincaid grade (family kid limit 5.0) with short sentences in everyday words; lab cards are two to seven words for a grown-up to read aloud to a 4 to 5 year old. Adult text averages 8.2 (limit 10) while naming stethoscope, otoscope, digital thermometer, milk teeth and check-up intervals precisely.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph does one job (why we go, who stays and asking, what the tools do, telling and calming). Adult paragraphs give curriculum and NHS/NICE placement, what happens in a visit with the tools, the named mistakes with the body-safety point, and what the lab does. No content-gate filler phrase matches.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes before and after Show me: the reason card and Yes/No boxes fit with wrapped sorted cards, the 2 by 2 visit cards and four numbered slots fit, the body diagram leaves room for four chips with leader lines and the tool tray below, five teeth fit across with the mirror above, and the worry meter and six action cards fit in a 2 by 3 grid. Buttons below the canvas wrap with large tap targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Yes/No with the card text in the label, one button per visit card, one per body place naming the tool, Keep still and Hand up, and one per worry-meter action. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, and right and wrong cards carry check and cross text as well as colour. walk.cjs runs axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13.
